description: State-issued contractor license number for parties who are licensed contractors (e.g., restoration vendors). Populated only when license_type is 'contractor'. Used in claims vendor management.
reference: State DOI; State Contractor Licensing Board

description: Timestamp when this license record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GDPR/CCPA record-keeping obligations.
Free-text description of any regulatory disciplinary actions, fines, or sanctions associated with this license. Populated only when disciplinary_action_indicator is True.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Indicates whether the licensee has any regulatory disciplinary actions, fines, or sanctions on record with the issuing DOI (True) or not (False). Sourced from NIPR PDB.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Date from which this license record is considered effective in the insurer's systems. May differ from issue_date if the license was backdated or loaded from a historical feed.
Name of the insurance carrier providing the licensee's Errors and Omissions (E&O) professional liability coverage. Required for producer appointment eligibility verification.
reference: State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

business_glossary_term: Errors and Omissions (E&O) Policy Expiry Date
description: Expiration date of the licensee's Errors and Omissions (E&O) professional liability policy. Drives alerts when E&O coverage is about to lapse, which may affect appointment status.
reference: State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Policy number of the licensee's Errors and Omissions (E&O) professional liability insurance. Verified during producer appointment and renewal processes.
reference: State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Number of ethics-specific continuing education (CE) credit hours completed by the licensee in the current renewal cycle. Compared against ethics_ce_credits_required.
reference: State DOI; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Number of ethics-specific continuing education (CE) credit hours mandated by the issuing state within the renewal cycle. Many states require a separate ethics CE component.
reference: State DOI; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Date on which this license expires and must be renewed to remain valid. Null for licenses with no fixed expiration. Drives renewal workflow and appointment eligibility.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Federal Employer Identification Number of the licensed entity when the licensee is an organization (agency or firm). Used for tax reporting and IRS compliance.
Indicates whether this is a resident (home-state) license (True) or a non-resident license (False). Non-resident licenses are issued under reciprocity agreements.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Date on which the issuing state DOI originally granted this license. Used to calculate license tenure and continuing education (CE) cycle start.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Two-letter US state or territory code of the Department of Insurance that issued this license (e.g., CA, TX, NY). Aligns with NAIC state coding standards.
Current regulatory status of the license as reported by the issuing DOI or NIPR. Drives eligibility for producer appointments and claim adjuster assignments.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Category of professional license held by the party. Distinguishes producer, adjuster, contractor, surplus lines, and other license types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product if types expand]
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Laws; State DOI

description: Date on which this license record was last verified against the NIPR Producer Database (PDB). Supports ongoing compliance monitoring and stale-data detection.
Result of the most recent NIPR PDB verification check for this license. 'mismatch' indicates discrepancies between internal records and NIPR data requiring remediation.
Free-text field for underwriting or compliance notes related to this license record, such as conditions, restrictions, or manual override explanations. For internal use only.
Unique National Producer Number assigned by NIPR to identify a licensed producer across all states. Used for cross-state appointment validation and NIPR PDB lookups.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Official license number assigned by the issuing state Department of Insurance (DOI) or regulatory authority. Used for NIPR validation and DOI compliance checks.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Laws; State DOI

description: Comma-delimited list of two-letter state codes where this license is recognized under reciprocity agreements. Enables multi-state appointment eligibility without separate applications.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act; State DOI

description: Date on which the license was most recently renewed by the issuing DOI. Tracks renewal history and supports continuing education (CE) compliance monitoring.
Two-letter US state code of the licensee's home state of residence. Distinguishes resident licenses from non-resident licenses for NIPR and reciprocity tracking.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Model Producer Licensing Act

description: Natural key or record identifier for this license in the originating source system (e.g., NIPR PDB record ID, PAS license record ID). Supports reconciliation and deduplication.

business_glossary_term: Social Security Number Last 4 Digits (SSN Last 4)
description: Last four digits of the licensee's Social Security Number, stored for identity verification purposes only. Full SSN must not be stored per GLBA and GDPR/CCPA data minimization.
Indicates whether the licensee is authorized to place surplus lines business in the issuing state (True) or not (False). Required for non-admitted market placements.
reference: State DOI; Surplus Lines Stamping Offices; NAIC Model Surplus Lines Law

description: State-issued surplus lines license number, distinct from the standard producer license number. Required for stamping office filings and surplus lines tax remittance.
reference: State DOI; Surplus Lines Stamping Offices

description: Date on which the license was terminated, revoked, or surrendered prior to its natural expiry. Null if the license has not been terminated. Required for DOI market conduct reporting.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Reason code explaining why the license was terminated or revoked. Populated only when termination_date is set. Supports regulatory and compliance reporting.
reference: NIPR; State DOI; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Timestamp when this license record was last modified in the data platform. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail compliance.
Unique surrogate identifier for each loss payee or mortgagee interest record. One row per interest attachment on a party and policy or insured risk.

Foreign key linking to coverage.coverage. Business justification: Loss payees (mortgagees, lienholders) are often specific to individual coverages rather than entire policies. Mortgagee on building coverage, lienholder on auto physical damage.
Foreign key linking to shared.currency. Business justification: Loss payee payment_threshold_amount and claim payments to lenders/mortgagees are currency-denominated.
Reference to the specific Insured Risk (property, vehicle, etc.) to which this loss payee interest is attached. Null when attached at policy level only.
Foreign key linking to party.address. Business justification: Loss payee embeds lender address fields that should be normalized to the address table. The address table is the SSOT for all addresses.
Reference to the Party record representing the lender, mortgagee, or loss payee entity holding the financial interest.
Reference to the Policy to which this loss payee interest is attached. Null when interest is attached at insured risk level only.
Foreign key linking to policy.term. Business justification: Loss payee interests (mortgagees, lienholders) are term-specific — they are added, changed, or removed by endorsement within a term.
ACORD standard form type used to evidence this loss payee or mortgagee interest (e.g., ACORD 25 Certificate of Liability, ACORD 28 Evidence of Property Insurance).
reference: ACORD Forms Library; ACORD Data Standards

description: Date on which the cancellation or non-renewal notice was sent to this loss payee or mortgagee. Required for regulatory compliance and audit.
reference: NAIC Model Cancellation Law; State DOI Regulations

description: Indicates whether the required cancellation or non-renewal notice has been sent to this loss payee or mortgagee per the policy terms and state regulations.
reference: NAIC Model Cancellation Law; State DOI Regulations

description: Date on which the Certificate of Insurance (CoI) was issued to this loss payee or mortgagee. Used for compliance tracking and renewal notifications.
Certificate of Insurance (CoI) number issued to this loss payee or mortgagee as evidence of coverage per ACORD 28 or equivalent form.
Timestamp when this loss payee interest record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and SOX compliance.
reference: SOX; NAIC Market Conduct Standards; GLBA

description: Date on which this loss payee or mortgagee interest becomes active and enforceable on the policy or insured risk.
reference: ACORD 28; NAIC Model Law; ISO Forms

description: Policy endorsement number under which this loss payee or mortgagee interest was added or modified on the policy.
Lender escrow account number used to collect and remit insurance premium payments on behalf of the mortgagor. Supports billing integration with lender.
reference: RESPA (Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act); GLBA; Guidewire BillingCenter

description: Date on which this loss payee or mortgagee interest expires or is removed. Null indicates the interest remains active through the policy term.
ISO or proprietary form number of the loss payable or mortgagee endorsement attached to the policy (e.g., ISO CP 12 18, PP 03 03).
reference: ISO Forms Library; ACORD Forms Library; DOI Filing

description: Ordinal rank of this interest when multiple loss payees or mortgagees exist on the same insured risk (e.g., first mortgagee = 1, second mortgagee = 2).
Current lifecycle status of the loss payee or mortgagee interest record. Drives whether the interest is honored in claims payment and certificate issuance.
Classification of the financial interest held by the party on the policy or insured risk. Drives certificate of insurance (CoI) and claims payment routing.
reference: ACORD 28 (Evidence of Property Insurance); ISO Forms; NAIC Model Law

description: Indicates whether claim payments must be made jointly to both the insured and this loss payee or mortgagee rather than solely to the insured.
reference: ISO CP 12 18; Mortgage Lending Standards; Guidewire ClaimCenter

description: Email address of the lender or mortgagee institution used for electronic certificate of insurance delivery and claims payment notifications.
IRS-assigned Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) of the lending institution. Required for tax reporting on claim payments and 1099 issuance.
Legal name of the lending institution, mortgagee, or lienholder as it must appear on the policy declarations and loss payment instruments.
Primary contact telephone number for the lender or mortgagee institution used for claims notification and certificate of insurance correspondence.
Secondary lender-assigned reference or account number (e.g., investor loan number, servicer reference) distinct from the primary loan number.
Lender-assigned loan or mortgage account number associated with the insured risk. Used to route claim payments and satisfy lender reporting requirements.
Type of loss payable clause attached to the policy for this interest: Standard, Lenders (protects lender independently), Open, or Union mortgage clause.
reference: ISO CP 12 18; ISO PP 03 03; ACORD Forms Library

business_glossary_term: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Lender Code
description: NAIC-assigned code identifying the lender or financial institution for statutory reporting and Schedule F bordereaux purposes.
Free-text underwriter or policy service notes regarding special conditions, lender instructions, or exceptions applicable to this loss payee interest.
Number of days advance notice required to be given to the lender or mortgagee before policy cancellation or non-renewal takes effect.
reference: NAIC Model Cancellation & Nonrenewal Law; ISO CP 12 18; State DOI Regulations

description: Indicates whether the lender or mortgagee must be notified of policy changes, cancellations, or non-renewals per the loss payable clause or lender agreement.
reference: ACORD 28; NAIC Model Cancellation Law; ISO CP 12 18

description: Full legal name(s) as they must appear on claim payment instruments (checks or EFT) issued jointly or solely to this loss payee or mortgagee.
reference: ACORD 28; Guidewire ClaimCenter; State DOI Regulations

description: Minimum claim payment amount above which joint payee or mortgagee co-endorsement is required per the lender agreement or loss payable clause.
reference: Mortgage Lending Standards; Guidewire ClaimCenter; ACORD 28

description: Indicates whether the insurance premium is billed directly to the lender via escrow rather than to the policyholder. Drives billing system routing.
reference: RESPA; Guidewire BillingCenter; ACORD Data Standards

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this loss payee interest record originated (e.g., PAS for PolicyCenter, MDM for Party Master).
reference: Guidewire PolicyCenter; Duck Creek Policy; ACORD Data Standards

description: Native identifier of this loss payee interest record in the originating operational system (e.g., Guidewire PolicyCenter internal ID) for lineage and reconciliation.
reference: Guidewire PolicyCenter; Duck Creek Policy; Data Lineage Standards

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this loss payee interest record. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and downstream incremental processing.
reference: SOX; NAIC Market Conduct Standards; GLBA

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each address record in the party domain. Primary key. One row per address per party.

Foreign key linking to catastrophegeography.cat_zone. Business justification: Underwriting eligibility decisions, moratorium enforcement, and concentration management require direct cat_zone assignment to addresses.
Reference to the party (person or organization) that owns this address. Links address to the Party master record.

business_glossary_term: Association for Cooperative Operations Research and Development (ACORD) Address Type Code
description: ACORD standard address type code from the ACORD data dictionary. Enables interoperability with ACORD 125/126/140 forms and carrier/agency data exchanges.
Current operational status of the address record. Active addresses receive policy documents and billing. Returned_mail triggers address update workflow in the PAS.
Classifies the purpose of the address: mailing for correspondence, billing for invoices, risk for insured property location, garaging for auto, loss for claim site.
In-care-of name for mail delivery when correspondence is directed through a third party (e.g., attorney, trustee, mortgagee). Common for additional insured notices.
US Census Bureau census tract code for the address. Used for demographic risk analysis, CRA compliance, and actuarial territory segmentation in pricing models.
reference: US Census Bureau; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: City or municipality name of the address. Used for territory rating, catastrophe aggregation, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
Flags whether the address is within a defined coastal zone subject to enhanced windstorm, storm surge, or tidal flood exposure. Used in underwriting eligibility screening.
reference: ISO Catastrophe Modeling; State DOI Coastal Zone Regulations

description: US Congressional district code for the address. Used for regulatory reporting, legislative tracking, and state DOI jurisdictional filings.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code (e.g., USA, CAN). Required for international policies, reinsurance bordereaux, and IFRS 17 reporting.
County or parish name for the address. Used for territory rating, surplus lines stamping, local tax jurisdiction, and catastrophe exposure aggregation.
reference: ISO Territory Rating; NAIC Annual Statement; Surplus Lines Stamping Offices

description: Timestamp when this address record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX/MAR compliance for record creation tracking.
reference: SOX; NAIC Model Audit Rule (MAR); GLBA

description: Straight-line distance in miles from the address to the nearest coastline. Used in windstorm rating, coastal surcharge calculation, and catastrophe model inputs.
reference: ISO Windstorm Rating; RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone

description: Distance in miles from the address to the nearest responding fire station. Used in ISO PPC determination and property rating for rural or semi-rural locations.
reference: ISO Public Protection Classification (PPC); ISO ERC

description: Suppresses physical mail delivery to this address per party preference or returned mail. Compliance with GLBA and state DOI notice delivery requirements.
reference: GLBA; State DOI Notice Requirements; NAIC Model Laws

description: USPS DPV result: Y=confirmed deliverable, S=primary match only, D=default match, N=not confirmed. Validates address deliverability for policy documents and billing.
Date from which this address record is valid for the party. Supports point-in-time reconstruction of the address in force at policy inception or loss date.
reference: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Model Laws; SAP/SSAP

description: Date on which this address record ceases to be valid. Null indicates currently active. Enables historical address reconstruction for claims and regulatory audits.
reference: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Model Laws; SAP/SSAP

description: Five-digit FIPS county code (2-digit state + 3-digit county). Used for catastrophe modeling, PML aggregation, and regulatory geographic reporting.
reference: FIPS PUB 6-4; NAIC; RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone

description: ISO Public Protection Classification (PPC) code (1-10) for the address. Directly impacts property insurance rating; class 1 is best, 10 is unprotected.
reference: ISO Public Protection Classification (PPC); ISO ERC

description: Precision level of the geocoded coordinates. Rooftop is highest precision; zip_centroid is lowest. Drives confidence weighting in catastrophe PML and AAL models.
reference: RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone; ISO Catastrophe Modeling

description: Name of the geocoding service or vendor that produced the latitude/longitude (e.g., Google Maps API, HERE, TomTom, ESRI). Supports data lineage and quality audits.
ISO-assigned rating territory code for this address. Used by the rating engine to apply territory-specific loss costs and rate factors per ISO circulars.
reference: ISO Rating Territory Definitions; ISO ERC/Earnix

description: Geographic latitude coordinate in decimal degrees (WGS84). Enables precise catastrophe hazard scoring, PML modeling, and territory assignment for insured locations.
reference: WGS84; RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone; ISO Catastrophe Modeling

description: Primary street address line including house/building number and street name. Used for mail delivery, risk location identification, and regulatory filings.
reference: USPS Publication 28; ACORD Data Standards; GLBA

description: Secondary address line for suite, apartment, unit, floor, or building designator. Supplements address_line1 for complete delivery address.
Geographic longitude coordinate in decimal degrees (WGS84). Paired with latitude for precise catastrophe hazard scoring and exposure aggregation.
reference: WGS84; RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone; ISO Catastrophe Modeling

description: Post Office box number when the mailing address is a PO Box rather than a street address. Used for billing and correspondence when party does not receive street delivery.
Non-US postal code for international addresses (e.g., Canadian postal code, UK postcode). Distinct from zip_code which is US-specific. Used for international risk rating.
Flags this as the primary address for the party when multiple addresses of the same type exist. Exactly one address per party per type should be primary at any time.
Province or region name for non-US addresses (e.g., Canadian provinces, Mexican states). Required for international policies and IFRS 17 geographic segmentation.
Indicates the address is a seasonal or secondary residence (e.g., vacation home). Relevant for homeowners underwriting, vacancy conditions, and occupancy rating.
Native address identifier from the originating operational system (e.g., Guidewire internal ID). Enables reconciliation between the lakehouse and the system of record.
Two-letter US state or territory code (USPS abbreviation). Drives regulatory jurisdiction, rate filings, DOI compliance, and statutory reporting by state.
reference: USPS Publication 28; NAIC State Reporting; DOI

description: IANA time zone identifier for the address location (e.g., America/New_York). Used for loss date/time determination, FNOL timestamping, and notice deadline calculations.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; NAIC Model Laws

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this address record. Used for change data capture, MDM deduplication refresh, and audit trail in the party data domain.
reference: SOX; NAIC Model Audit Rule (MAR); Customer/Party MDM

description: Indicates whether the address has been validated and standardized against the USPS Coding Accuracy Support System (CASS). Ensures deliverability and geocoding accuracy.
Indicates whether this address falls within a state wind pool or FAIR plan territory (e.g., Texas Windstorm, Florida Citizens). Affects coverage eligibility and reinsurance.
reference: State DOI Wind Pool Regulations; ISO Catastrophe Modeling

description: Five-digit US ZIP code for the address. Used for territory rating, catastrophe zone assignment, and USPS mail delivery routing.
Four-digit ZIP+4 extension providing carrier route precision for USPS delivery. Enhances geocoding accuracy for catastrophe modeling and territory rating.
reference: USPS Publication 28; RMS RiskLink; Verisk AIR Touchstone

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each contact point record in the party contact master. One row per contact point per party.
Reference to the Party record that owns this contact point. Links contact to the party master for identity resolution and KYC.
ACORD standard contact type code from the ACORD data dictionary (e.g., ACORD 125/126 PhoneInfo/EmailInfo type codes). Enables interoperability with trading partners.
Latest time of day (HH:MM, 24-hour local) the party prefers to be contacted via this channel. Supports TCPA-compliant outbound call scheduling.
Earliest time of day (HH:MM, 24-hour local) the party prefers to be contacted via this channel. Supports TCPA-compliant outbound call scheduling.
Channel or mechanism through which opt-in consent was captured (e.g., web_form, agent_recorded, ivr, written). Supports GLBA and TCPA audit trail requirements.
Current lifecycle status of this contact point. Bounced indicates delivery failure; opted_out reflects GLBA/TCPA suppression. Drives communication eligibility.
Classification of the communication channel for this contact point (e.g., phone, email, fax, sms, postal_address, web_portal). Drives routing in PAS and CMS.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code associated with this contact point. Used for international dialing prefix resolution and regulatory jurisdiction mapping.
Timestamp when this contact point record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, GLBA data retention, and MDM lineage requirements.
Hard suppression flag indicating the party must not be contacted via this channel regardless of opt-in status. Overrides all outbound communication triggers.
reference: GLBA; TCPA; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Reason code explaining why the do_not_contact_flag is set. Supports legal hold, regulatory order, and SIU fraud investigation suppression scenarios.
reference: GLBA; NAIC Market Conduct Standards; SOX

description: Date from which this contact point is considered active and valid for the party. Supports point-in-time reconstruction of contact data for policy and claims history.
Structured email address for the party when contact_type is email. Stored separately for validation, opt-in tracking, and GLBA compliance.
reference: GLBA; GDPR Article 4; CCPA; CAN-SPAM Act

description: SMTP bounce code or classification (e.g., 550 hard bounce, 421 soft bounce) returned when an email delivery attempt failed. Used to update contact_status to bounced.
Date on which this contact point ceases to be valid. Null indicates the contact point is currently active. Enables temporal querying of contact history.
Indicates whether this is the party's overall preferred contact method across all contact types. Used by PAS and CMS to select the default outreach channel.
Indicates whether this contact point is the primary contact for the party within its contact_type. Only one record per party per contact_type should be primary.
Indicates whether a phone contact point has been confirmed as a mobile/wireless number via carrier lookup. Critical for TCPA autodialer and text message compliance.
Indicates whether the phone number is a wireless (cell) number as determined by carrier lookup. Distinct from is_verified_mobile; set by automated number type detection.
Preferred language for communications via this contact point in BCP 47 format (e.g., en-US, es-MX). Supports state DOI language access requirements.
reference: State DOI Language Access Requirements; ACORD Data Standards

description: Most recent date on which a successful outbound or inbound communication was recorded via this contact point. Used for contact recency analytics and dormancy detection.
Result of the most recent communication attempt via this contact point (e.g., reached, no_answer, voicemail, bounced). Informs next-best-action in claims and billing.
reference: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Free-text notes recorded by an agent or adjuster about this contact point (e.g., call-back instructions, seasonal address). Stored in PAS and CMS contact objects.
Indicates whether the party has affirmatively opted in to receive communications via this contact point. Required for GLBA and TCPA compliance tracking.
Date and time when the party provided opt-in consent for this contact point. Retained as evidence of consent for GLBA and TCPA regulatory audits.
Indicates whether the party has explicitly opted out of communications via this contact point. Suppresses outbound contact in PAS, CMS, and Billing systems.
Date and time when the party revoked consent or opted out for this contact point. Triggers suppression in all downstream communication systems.
Optional telephone extension appended to the phone number for commercial parties, brokers, or agency contacts in the Producer Management System.
Structured phone number in E.164 format for the party when contact_type is phone or sms. Used for FNOL intake, billing, and claims communication.
Native identifier of this contact record in the originating operational system (e.g., Guidewire ContactID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and MDM deduplication.

Secondary classification refining the contact type (e.g., home, work, mobile, billing, claims, underwriting). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: home|work|mobile|billing|claims|underwriting|other — promote to reference product]
IANA time zone identifier for this contact point (e.g., America/New_York). Used to schedule compliant outbound calls within TCPA permitted calling hours.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this contact point record. Used for change data capture, MDM synchronization, and audit trail compliance.
Business purpose for which this contact point is used (e.g., billing notices, claims FNOL, policy documents, marketing). Drives targeted communication routing.
reference: GLBA; ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: The actual contact point value: phone number, email address, fax number, SMS number, or postal address string depending on contact_type. Contains PII.
Date on which the contact point was last verified through a validation process such as email ping, carrier lookup, or agent confirmation.
Method used to verify this contact point (e.g., carrier_lookup for phone, email_ping for email, agent_confirmed for manual review). Supports MDM data quality.
Indicates whether this contact point has been validated (e.g., email deliverability check, phone number validation via carrier lookup). Used in KYC and MDM.
reference: NAIC Model Laws; Customer/Party MDM; GLBA

description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying one party identifier record. One row per identifier per party. Grain: one row per external or internal identifier assigned to a party.

business_glossary_term: Master Data Management (MDM) Golden Party ID
description: The MDM golden record identifier assigned to the party after deduplication and survivorship processing. Links this identifier to the authoritative master party record across all source systems.
reference: MDM Best Practices; GLBA; ACORD Data Standards

description: Reference to the party record that owns this identifier. Links the identifier back to the master party in the Customer/Party MDM.
The party identifier as assigned by the Policy Administration System (Guidewire PolicyCenter or Duck Creek Policy). Used for cross-reference between the data lakehouse and the PAS.
reference: Guidewire PolicyCenter; Duck Creek Policy; ACORD Data Standards

description: Foreign key linking to party.license. Business justification: The identifier table stores raw external identifier values (license numbers, NPNs, SSNs, TINs) as typed records, while the license table stores the full structured license entity with status

business_glossary_term: Comprehensive Loss Underwriting Exchange (CLUE) Report Ordered Flag
description: Indicates whether a CLUE (Comprehensive Loss Underwriting Exchange) report has been ordered for this party identifier. Used in personal lines underwriting to retrieve prior loss history.
reference: FCRA; LexisNexis CLUE; ISO A-PLUS; NAIC Underwriting Guidelines

description: Timestamp when this identifier record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX; GLBA; NAIC Annual Statement; SAP/SSAP

description: Normalized, standardized form of the identifier value used for fuzzy matching and deduplication in the Party MDM. Strips formatting characters (dashes, spaces) for consistent comparison.
reference: MDM Best Practices; GLBA; ACORD Data Standards

description: Date on which this identifier became valid and effective. Used for temporal queries to determine which identifier was active at a given point in time.
reference: ACORD Data Standards; NAIC Model Laws

description: Date on which this identifier expires or ceases to be valid. Null for identifiers with no expiry (e.g., SSN, FEIN). Used for license renewal tracking and compliance monitoring.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Market Conduct Standards; AAMVA

description: Flag set by the Fraud Detection/SIU system indicating this identifier has been associated with suspected or confirmed fraudulent activity. Triggers enhanced review in underwriting and claims.
reference: NAIC Market Conduct Standards; NICB; SIU Best Practices; FCRA

description: Current lifecycle status of this identifier record: active (in use), inactive (superseded), expired (past validity), revoked (cancelled by issuing authority), pending_verification (awaiting confirmation).
Indicates whether the identifier_value stored is a masked or tokenized representation rather than the full plaintext value. True when only last-4 digits or a token is stored for PCI/GLBA compliance.
reference: GLBA; GDPR Article 25; CCPA; PCI DSS

description: Indicates whether this is the primary identifier for the party within its identifier type. True if this is the preferred or golden record identifier used for cross-system matching and deduplication.
reference: ACORD Data Standards; MDM Best Practices

description: Name of the government agency, regulatory body, or internal system that issued this identifier (e.g., IRS, SSA, NIPR, state DMV, state DOI, NAIC, internal MDM system).
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country that issued this identifier (e.g., USA, CAN, GBR). Required for passports and foreign national identifiers.
Two-letter US state or territory code of the jurisdiction that issued this identifier. Applicable for driver licenses, state-issued producer licenses, and state DOI registrations.
reference: USPS State Abbreviations; NAIC; NIPR; AAMVA

description: Know Your Customer compliance status for this identifier as part of anti-money laundering and fraud screening. Tracks whether the identifier has passed identity verification per GLBA and BSA/AML requirements.
reference: GLBA; BSA/AML; FinCEN; OFAC; NAIC Market Conduct Standards

description: Classification of the license associated with this identifier (e.g., producer license class: P&C, Life, Health; driver license class: A, B, C, M). Applicable for DLN and producer license identifier types.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act; AAMVA; State DOI

description: Two-letter US state code of the jurisdiction under which the license was issued. Distinct from issuing_state_code when a producer holds licenses in multiple states.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act; State DOI; USPS

description: Partially masked display version of the identifier for UI and reporting use (e.g., ***-**-1234 for SSN, **-***1234 for FEIN). Allows display without exposing the full sensitive value.
reference: GLBA; GDPR Article 25; CCPA; PCI DSS

description: Date on which the most recent MVR was ordered for this driver license identifier. Used to determine MVR currency and whether a refresh is required per underwriting guidelines.
reference: FCRA; AAMVA; DPPA; NAIC Auto Underwriting Guidelines

description: Indicates whether a Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) has been ordered for this driver license identifier. Applicable when identifier_type_code = DLN. Used in personal and commercial auto underwriting.
reference: FCRA; AAMVA; DPPA (Driver Privacy Protection Act); NAIC

business_glossary_term: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Company Code
description: Five-digit NAIC company code assigned to an insurance carrier or reinsurer. Populated when identifier_type_code = NAIC_CODE. Used in statutory reporting and Schedule F/P filings.
reference: NAIC Annual Statement; NAIC Company Database; SAP/SSAP

description: Free-text notes or comments recorded by underwriters, compliance officers, or MDM stewards regarding this identifier (e.g., reason for revocation, manual override justification, discrepancy notes).
reference: NAIC Market Conduct Standards; SOX; MDM Best Practices

description: NIPR-assigned National Producer Number for licensed insurance producers and agencies. Populated when identifier_type_code = NPN. Required for producer appointment and commission processing.
reference: NIPR; NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act; State DOI regulations

business_glossary_term: Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Check Status
description: Result of OFAC SDN (Specially Designated Nationals) screening for this identifier. Required for sanctions compliance. Cleared = no match; Flagged = potential match requiring review.
